ASTRA — A NEW INVESTIGATION INTO COMPUTABLE LONG-TIME PHYSICS
1 November 2026

RESULT

I constructed a conditional computational principle for long-time physical response:
use an exactly tractable INTERACTING reference process, retain its full dynamical
memory algebraically, and calculate bounded nonintegrable changes through scalar
operator-insertion moments. The reference is not required to be a collection of
independent particles, and the calculation does not require a compressible full
many-body solution vector.

The central theorem supplies controlled mean first-arrival times and equilibrium
Poisson responses. At fixed locality, kinetic contrast and accuracy, its formal work
is polynomial in system size and polylogarithmic in the reference spectral stiffness.
I constructed the reference, the perturbative scalar contraction, ordinary proofs,
finite numerical checks, a large reference calculation, a large first-insertion
calculation, and a high-precision stiffness failure/recovery.

This is a bounded mathematical opening. I have NOT established the requested
civilisation-changing foundation, historical novelty, a general molecular simulator,
or a total practical advantage over the strongest existing methods. Strong positive
competitors repeatedly changed the question and remain included. The next serious
obstruction is the number of interaction words needed for extensive or strongly
nonintegrable matter, not an unmeasured molecular helper.

THE CONSEQUENTIAL QUESTION

Can long-time changes and low-frequency response of interacting matter be calculated
from microscopic laws without storing its exponentially large state space or
simulating every fast event through its slowest relaxation time?

A broad solution would improve the ability to predict aging, collective assembly,
fluctuations and transport before waiting for those processes. That broad capability
is not supplied by the present one-dimensional model. The construction is intended
as a possible mathematical bridge, with the limits kept explicit.

1 November 2026

Decision
========
This branch does not presently establish a civilization-changing advance.
It positively constructs several stronger conventional routes, and therefore
rejects "bypass slow spin sampling to calculate thermodynamics" as an adequate
new question by itself. The surviving obstruction is not just nonplanarity,
frustration, or pairwise microscopic interactions. It is the global contraction
of genuinely many-port boundary actions, or prediction of dynamics after an
equilibrium-preserving representation change.

There is reusable mathematical capital: an explicit real, zero-field, four-
auxiliary quartic interaction; a linear-size even-parity compiler at one chosen
temperature with explicit coupling growth; and a precise no-go for exact
temperature-independent Hamiltonian emulation across a temperature interval.
These are independently derived constructions, not verified priority claims.
The broad ideas of decoration, exact many-spin compilation, and altered-space
cluster sampling are established. A smaller gadget alone is not the mandate.

Files
=====
planar_equilibrium.py: independent Kac–Ward solver, enumeration comparison,
field-response and low-temperature numerical failure tests.
planar_results.json: exact execution record, including random seed and timings.
boundary_compilation.py: exact local sums, Walsh interaction extraction,
frustrated-module reduction and finite-temperature parity-tree resources.
boundary_results.json: execution record.

Run with Python, NumPy and SciPy, for example:
  OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python planar_equilibrium.py
  OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python boundary_compilation.py
No research repository code was copied into either implementation.

===============================================

# Resolved classical reaction records: an existing matchgate construction

Root considered retaining a full conditional Gaussian probability vector while observing selected individual reaction channels and applying causal feedback. The following constructive conventional route displaces a foundational novelty claim for that closure. It does not invoke quantum Born probabilities.

## Local algebra

For nearest-neighbor pair creation `00->11` at c, annihilation `11->00` at a, and hopping `10->01` at d, `01->10` at e, the column generator in basis 00,01,10,11 is

    q = [[-c,  0,  0,  a],
         [ 0, -e,  d,  0],
         [ 0,  e, -d,  0],
         [ c,  0,  0, -a]].

Its even and odd block traces are equal precisely when `a+c=d+e`. Hence `exp(t q)` has parity blocks of equal determinant, the standard matchgate condition. Removing an observed channel's off-diagonal jump matrix J leaves the diagonal unchanged, so `q0=q-sum J` retains this trace equality and quadratic fermion form. A sum over bonds is still a quadratic global generator; its propagator is a Gaussian linear map. A periodic boundary requires its actual parity-sector sign.

Each individually resolved jump matrix `J=r|out><in|` within one parity sector is a singular matchgate: both 2x2 block determinants vanish. Equivalently it is a product of two linear creation/annihilation operators (including the required JW sign). Applying such a map to a pure fermionic Gaussian amplitude vector retains that class, possibly with a different Gaussian chart. Single-chart BCS coordinates may become singular; that is a representation issue, not permission to discard the event.

## The classical normalization is also a Gaussian contraction

On a fixed even-parity sector, define the unnormalized bra

    <Omega| = <0| exp(sum_(i<j) c_j c_i).

Its coefficient on every even occupancy set I is `Pf(S_I)`, where `S_ij=1` for i<j and `S_ji=-1`. This Pfaffian is 1 for every even I: expand in the first row; the alternating sum of 2k-1 ones is 1, and induct on k. Consequently `<Omega|p>` is exactly the sum of the classical probabilities, with no squaring of amplitudes. An extra auxiliary mode handles odd parity, or two parity components can be carried separately.

For an observed record with marked jumps a_1,...,a_m at times t_1,...,t_m, its likelihood density is the ordinary contraction

    <Omega| exp(Q0*(T-t_m)) J_(a_m)
